variants.name: TypeORM version column
variants.implementation_notes: TypeORM tracks the token in the entity: a @VersionColumn() property is set to the entity's version on every save, so the generated UPDATE carries the version predicate and a stale save raises OptimisticLockVersionMismatchError. Queries can also request the check explicitly with lock: { mode: 'optimistic', version: n }. The classic structure is replaced by the decorated column plus the repository's save path; bulk query-builder statements do not run through it.
pitfalls: Bulk paths (repository.update(), query-builder updates, raw SQL) do not carry the version column, so they must be treated as escape hatches and excluded from the guarded model.
The explicit optimistic lock mode needs the version the query should expect (lock: { mode: 'optimistic', version }); omitting it turns the read into an unchecked one.
TypeScript's structural typing lets a DTO satisfy the entity type without the version property - loading records into DTOs and saving them back is how unguarded writes appear.

variants.name: ETag + If-Match conditional request
variants.idiom_name: If-Match request header against the resource ETag
variants.implementation_notes: At the HTTP boundary the token is the ETag: the client reads the resource (and its ETag), later sends the mutation with If-Match: "<etag>", and the server compares with the strong comparison algorithm, answering 412 Precondition Failed when the representation changed - MDN names preventing the lost-update problem as the primary use case. The validator is then the same token mechanism with the version in a header and the conflict as a status code, which makes it the natural TypeScript/fetch form for offline-capable web clients.
pitfalls: Weak validators (W/ prefixed ETags) never satisfy If-Match because the comparison is strong - marking a version ETag weak silently disables the guard.
The ETag must change on every state mutation; caches or proxies that normalize/recompute it can let two different states share a token.
412 must be handled as a conflict (re-fetch, merge, bounded retry), not as a generic error - retrying the same request unchanged fails again.
